sources.entry: ralph-harness by Vitaly Kuprin - A CLI that runs Claude Code in a loop, with a fresh claude -p process for each iteration in a harness-owned git worktree.

summary.one_liner: A Bun-based CLI that runs Claude Code in a long-lived loop, starting a fresh `claude -p` process per iteration inside a harness-owned git worktree, and only shipping commits that pass git, your VERIFY_CMD, FROZEN paths and a read-only reviewer.
use_cases: Run a Claude Code agent unattended for many hours on a coding job
Gate AI-generated commits behind tests and a reviewer before they are pushed
Open one pull request that collects all of an agent's kept commits
Keep an autonomous agent from touching frozen paths or your own checkout
Resume an agent loop automatically after usage limits
Steer or stop a running background agent loop from the terminal
how_to_run: git clone https://github.com/vkuprin/ralph-harness && cd ralph-harness && ln -s "$PWD/bin/ralph" ~/.local/bin/ralph
ralph edit audit && ralph start audit && ralph status
stack: gh (GitHub CLI, used for pull requests)
notable: Each iteration is a fresh claude -p process; state carries over only via PROMPT.md and PROGRESS.md
The harness, not the agent, pushes; reset commits are kept under refs/ralph for inspection
Usage-limit waits do not count toward MAX_ITER and time asleep does not count toward timeouts
Hard constraints are numbered pass/fail tests that the reviewer enforces and the agent cannot loosen
Native Windows support via Git Bash, with a ralph.stop file for graceful stop
caveats: The agent runs with --dangerously-skip-permissions, so the README advises running it in a container or VM without production credentials
Dollar figures reported are API-equivalent estimates and a lower bound, not subscription bills
On Windows, the npm claude.cmd wrapper is refused; the native claude.exe build is required
